draft.title: Significant figures and rounding
card: Significant figures (sf) count digits from the first non-zero digit. In 0.004 706, the first sf is 4, so the number has 4 sf: 4, 7, 0, 6.
To round, find the last digit you keep and look at the next digit. If it is 5 or more, round up. If it is 4 or less, leave the last digit as it is.
Decimal places (dp) count digits after the decimal point. Zeros that only hold the place value are not significant, and leading zeros never count.
Example: 38 462 to 2 sf. The first two digits are 3 and 8. The next digit is 4, so we do not round up. Fill the rest with zeros: 38 000.
draft.remember: Count sf from the first non-zero digit. Look one digit past where you stop.

a.q: What is 0.07382 rounded to 2 significant figures?
a.why: The first sf is 7, so the two sf are 7 and 3. The next digit is 8, so round the 3 up to 4, giving 0.074. The answer 0.073 forgets to round up.
a.clue: Start counting at the first non-zero digit.

b.q: A tile measures 2.0496 m long. What is this to 3 significant figures?
b.why: The three sf are 2, 0 and 4, and the next digit is 9, so the 4 rounds up to 5. This gives 2.05 m. The answer 2.04 m cuts off the number without rounding. The answer 2.050 m has 4 sf.
b.clue: A zero between two non-zero digits counts.

proposal.title: Significant figures and rounding
card: Significant figures (sf) are counted from the first non-zero digit, so leading zeros never count. 0.004 706 has 4 sf: 4, 7, 0, 6. The zero between 7 and 6 counts.
To round, find the last digit you keep and look at the next digit. If it is 5 or more, round up. If it is 4 or less, leave the last digit as it is.
Decimal places (dp) count every digit after the decimal point, zeros included, so 0.004 706 has 6 dp. Use dp when the job needs a fixed unit, such as 2 dp for dollars and cents.
Example: 38 462 to 2 sf. The first two digits are 3 and 8. The next digit is 4, so we do not round up: 38 000. These zeros only hold place value, so they are not significant.
proposal.remember: Count sf from the first non-zero digit. Look one digit past where you stop.
